title: Vendor selection briefing — capacity sourcing
content:
Executive summary:
This brief prepares GTM and field teams for enterprise procurement conversations focused on dedicated inference capacity: predictable throughput, tenant isolation, and SLA-backed guarantees. It bundles a buyer-facing narrative, a procurement scoring rubric, suggested contract clauses, and a short negotiation playbook. Goal: reduce procurement friction, speed contracts, and create repeatable evidence we can hand to platform and legal buyers during evaluation.

Purpose and context:
- Audience: procurement, platform engineering (architects), SRE, finance, and security buyers.
- Why now: customers evaluating dedicated capacity cite three fast blockers — uncertain throughput, lack of formal isolation guarantees, and unclear remediation/credits when capacity misses targets.
- Outcome: give sales and solutions teams concise, procurement-oriented materials and a repeatable checklist to accelerate purchase decisions.

One-line positioning for procurement decks:
"Committed GPU capacity with isolation guarantees and measurable latency & throughput SLAs — so platform teams get predictable unit economics and legal teams get contractable remedies."

Buyer personas + tailored messages:
- Platform architect / infra lead: "We deliver pinned compute+network paths, KV cache persistence options, and throughput commitments so engineering can meet SLOs without overprovisioning. Here are the acceptance tests and perf artifacts you can run."
- Procurement / Sourcing: "We offer committed monthly capacity with clear overage pricing, trial-to-commit conversion steps, and SLA credit mechanics — purchase terms that map to your capacity planning windows."
- Security / CISO: "Private control plane, customer-managed VPC peering, KMS-integrated keying, and optional air-gapped on-prem packaging for regulated workloads."
- CFO / Finance: "Predictable spend profile (committed vs burst), optional annual prepay with discount bands, and per-token cost ceilings for model families to cap marginal spend."

Procurement scoring rubric (recommended to give to buyers or internal AE guides):
Score buckets (0–5, higher is better) across:
- Predictability: Are throughput/latency commitments explicit and measurable? (evidence: benchmark runbooks, p95/p99 artifacts)
- Isolation: Is compute and network tenancy isolatable/encapsulated? (evidence: topology diagram + cryptographic controls)
- Remediation: Are credits/remedies defined for missed SLOs? (evidence: sample SLA schedule)
- Integration: Is onboarding time and cutover plan documented? (evidence: runbook + staging window)
- Commercial alignment: Are pricing and overage mechanics clear? (evidence: sample quote + T&Cs)
- Compliance: Certifications and controls for regulated data (SOC2, FedRAMP posture notes)

Example benchmark/acceptance tests to include in PO/SOW:
- Sustained throughput test: 3 hours at committed RPS for canonical model and request mix, P95 latency <= X ms, error rate < 0.2%.
- Cold-start tail: Simulated scale-up from 0 to committed instances with median scale-up time <= Y seconds.
- Failover & fallback: Simulated single-AZ failure with <5% request loss and automatic fallback to standby pool within Z seconds.
- KV-cache sweep: Validate cache warmup retention across typical session patterns for 24 hours without eviction above configured thresholds.

SLA definitions (proposal language snippets):
- Availability: "Committed cluster availability 99.9% monthly measured at per-customer cluster level; credit = monthly service fee * (1 - availability / 0.999)."
- Latency SLO: "For the committed model class and request profile, 95th percentile token generation latency <= X ms, 99th percentile <= Y ms (measured at our ingress). Missed SLOs trigger per-incident credits capped at Z% of monthly committed fees."
- Throughput guarantee: "Sustained throughput equal to declared committed RPS at specified concurrency with bounded degradation < A% during peak windows. Burstable capacity policy described in Annex A."
- Incident transparency: "Root cause, timeline, and corrective action plan delivered within 72 hours for any incident triggering SLA credits."

Isolation — what buyers ask for and what we can commit to:
- Types of isolation to make explicit: compute tenancy (dedicated VMs/GPU pods), network tenancy (VPC peering and NACL rules), control plane isolation (per-customer service accounts), and storage/data plane separation (customer-managed buckets + encryption).
- Practical ask we accept: dedicated tenant clusters with optional dedicated subnets; optional on-prem appliance (air-gapped) for highest assurance contracts.
- Implementation note: isolation increases cost; present cost delta as Delta% of committed base and show break-even analysis versus lost engineering time and SLO failures.

Commercial constructs — recommended options to present in quotes:
- Committed baseline (monthly GPUs / throughput) + buffer pool for burst (e.g., 10% burst included) + overage rate for delta.
- Annual prepay discounts: 10% for 12-month commit, 18% for 24-month, higher for larger $ commitments.
- Performance credits: % credit tiers for availability/latency misses; cap at e.g., 50% of monthly committed fee.

Negotiation playbook for reps (quick wins):
1) Start with data: provide a 48-hour dedicated perf trial for the customer's canonical workload. Capture P95/P99, error rate, and throughput curves.
2) Offer a clearly scoped staging window and acceptance tests (use the bench above). Attach them to the PO as SOW acceptance criteria.
3) For security-conscious buyers, propose a phased approach: start with dedicated VPC + encrypted storage, then propose on-prem/air-gapped if required after pilot.
4) Keep legal discussions focused: provide a short list of standard redlines we can accept vs. those requiring escalations (list attached as annex).

Common objections + suggested responses:
- "We can get cheaper GPUs elsewhere": "True; but compare net unit costs — when you factor in cache efficiency, batching library, and predictable tail latency, our committed+isolation option often reduces total cost of ownership by limiting overprovisioning and outages. We’ll show a 90-day run-rate comparison for your workload."
- "We need strict data residency": "We support region-specific clusters and private deployment packages with customer-managed networking. We’ll provide SOC2+audit artifacts and a SOC2 bridge for any gap remediation items."
- "What if performance regresses after model upgrades?": "We include controlled rollouts (canary A/B) and automatic fallback to pinned variants; quality regressions are covered by our Optimize telemetry and rollback policies included in the contract."

Competitive notes (short):
- Hyperscalers: strong on raw capacity and price at scale, weak on plug-and-play inference features (prefix caching, KV-aware runtime) and often require customer ops investment to hit low tail latencies.
- Self-hosted vendors: flexibility but high ops burden; buyers who lack SRE headcount prefer a managed dedicated SKU with SLAs.
- Inference incumbents: differentiate on predictable per-token economics + transparent profiling artifacts that map to procurement scoring criteria.

Legal/contract clauses to pre-populate for deal desks:
- Definition appendix: define "committed throughput", "burst capacity", and "availability" precisely.
- Credits schedule: explicit percent credit slabs tied to per-cluster availability and latency miss categories.
- Change control: changes to model families, request mix, or sequence length require re-run of acceptance tests and may trigger price adjustments.
- Termination for convenience / migration assistance: offer 60-day export window + assistance runbook for large customers migrating away.

Field assets to attach to quotes (recommended):
- Short perf packet: canonical workload runs with p95/p99 and throughput curves (CSV + summary).
- Acceptance test checklist and runbook (step-by-step).
- Topology diagram showing isolation layers.
- Sample contract excerpt with SLA schedule and credit calculator.

Next steps / owners:
- Create a one-page procurement cheat sheet derived from this brief for AEs (owner: Diego Martinez; due: 2025-11-22).
- Build a standardized perf-trial template and auto-attach it to quotes (owner: Marcus Liu; due: 2025-12-05).
- Legal: pre-approve a set of acceptable SLA credit tiers and redline matrix for typical platform buyers (owner: Priya Kapoor; due: 2025-12-12).

Appendix: quick sample pitch lines by buyer type (ready for slide/snippet use)
- Procurement: "We map committed throughput to a firm monthly cost and provide a simple credit schedule if SLOs miss — removes variability from your monthly run-rate."
- Platform lead: "Your app hits reproducible tail latency under bounded concurrency — we'll ship a staged rollout plan and acceptance tests you can run with your QA artifacts."
- CISO: "Customer-managed keys, VPC peering, and optional air-gapped package — we’ll provide audit evidence and a SOC bridge."

Notes to self: include links to INF-4217 perf-automation and the risk ladder spreadsheets before finalizing.

End of brief.
